title: ConnCollege vs Hamilton: tuition, size, location
summary: Connecticut College (ConnCollege) versus Hamilton College (Hamilton). Also searched as Hamilton vs ConnCollege. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Hamilton College and Connecticut College are both private nonprofit institutions, each with a similar undergraduate enrollment size, with Hamilton hosting approximately 2,030 students and Connecticut College about 1,937. Located in different cities, Hamilton is situated in Clinton, while Connecticut College is in New London. Tuition costs are comparable, with Hamilton charging $68,960 and Connecticut College slightly less at $67,242. These factors highlight some of the distinctions between Hamilton College vs Connecticut College, reflecting differences in location and tuition within the private nonprofit sector.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing Hamilton College vs Connecticut College in terms of cost, both institutions charge similar tuition rates for in-state and out-of-state students, with Hamilton's tuition at $68,960 and Connecticut College's at $67,242. Despite the close tuition figures, there is a notable difference in the median debt of students who complete their degrees. Hamilton graduates have a median debt of $17,000, whereas Connecticut College graduates carry a higher median debt of $23,500. These financial aspects are important considerations for prospective students evaluating Hamilton vs ConnCollege, as they reflect both the immediate cost of attendance and the long-term financial impact after graduation.
